In the window: hyperscaler Q3 calls (late Oct) with 2027 capex guides, which feed both the AI-compute trade and my price path (more capex means more 2027-28 supply); Nvidia's results (~19 Nov); possible Tesla-SpaceX merger news (Polymarket puts an announcement at 42.5% by Jun-27, so a November announcement is a low-probability two-sided event). Starship Flight 15 is 'just before Thanksgiving', probably just after the window (Manifold ~36% ship catch). The IPO lock-up (~180 days, ~Dec 9) falls after the window and may weigh into late November. Net: symmetric around ~$152, sigma ~19% (realised 82% is inflated after the IPO, so ~65% annual / 3.5).

comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The EV/EBITDA multiple is a mix, not a discount to one peer: ~80% of horizon NTM EBITDA is rent from GPUs with a 5-6 year life (424B4) on leases terminable on ~90 days' notice, at ~2x the NPV-0 new-build price, which is how neoclouds earn theirs (CRWV ~10x 2027 at a Buy target, lower traded); the rest (Starlink, launch, apps) is mega-cap-like at 16.1x. 0.8 x 8 + 0.2 x 16.1 = 9.6x. The industry evidence says the rent premium decays (2023-25 H100 -56-64%; 2027 capex and CoWoS supply jump), and that decay lasts through the horizon because the horizon buyer pays for 2028-32 rents. No P/E premium because FY29 EPS falls on my path. Fewer than 10 usable comparables carry forward data; there is no listed peer for the launch business.

thesis_break_reason: A close below ~$86 (18% under the $104.83 post-IPO low, ~43% below today and ~8% under my $93 fair value) would most likely mean the market has dropped the narrative premium and is pricing the early-fade state: rental indices (B300, SDH100RT) rolling over before mid-2027, lessees using their 90-day exits, renewals below ~$35/W-yr, or a 2027 build stalling for funding. My engine bear is ~$59 and the SOTP leg ~$52, so $86 is where the fundamental story, not ordinary volatility for an 82%-vol stock, is being repriced. On the upside my below-market view is wrong if renewals still clear above $45/W-yr in H2-27 while SpaceX adds ~0.5 GW a month.

reverse_dcf_check: 10x NTM EBITDA (~$175B) gives EV ~$1.75T at the horizon. At 9.19% and 15% RONIC on FY28 NOPAT of ~$91B that needs ~6% perpetual growth, which my fade to the NPV-0 price does not support (the SOTP worth of the same fleet is ~3x its EBITDA), so 10x already assumes Starlink and apps growth carry the business past the compute fade. Today's EV (~$2.0T on 12.84B economic shares plus EchoStar, less $51B net cash) needs ~$150B of steady-state NOPAT at 3% growth: roughly 13 GW at $45+/W-yr held into the 2030s, i.e. the 13 GW and hold paths together.

reasoning: Industry lane, round 2. (1) Facts I had wrong or missed (supervisor): Cursor awards were expensed AND in the share count (now counted once, via shares); Musk's 1,302M Mars/100 TW-conditioned shares are not economic (12,839M now, 13,166M at H); 'MS 8.3 GW' was not in the MS note (it models ~5 GW, pre-Q3), so it is dropped; Grain's $8B cash spectrum purchase was missing, so it is now an adjustment. (2) Shortage durability: the Q3 call has pricing 'slightly above the high end of $30-50 per watt' and renewals at higher $/W; Nebius raised H100/H200 prices 17-20% on 1-Oct; the B300 median is $9.50/hr. The indices are still rising, so I hold ~$52 through H1-27 and soften the fade to $48 (H2-27) and $40 (2028; was $35). The fade still comes: ~$1T of 2027 hyperscaler capex, CoWoS 190-200k wpm, and the 2024-25 H100 episode (-56-64% in ~a year). Then $31, $25, $21 and the NPV-0 $18.8 from 2032. The shortage lasts at full strength ~9 months from today and fades over 2028-31. (3) Capacity: 8.6 GW YE27 (was 8.0): the end-October step to ~2.2 GW and Musk's 200-220k GB300/month (~0.42 GW/month) plus Rubin wattage, against 13 GW, which needs ~0.85 GW/month and ~$385B of 2027 SI capex. Capex $38/W (2027), $39.5/W (2028). (4) Values: fleet $477B, window $28B, Starlink $264B, Space $54B (Starship odds cut after the cadence walk-back), Cursor $54B, X $10B: SOTP $52.35/sh. Multiples: 10x EV/EBITDA, kept and argued as a neocloud/mega-cap mix (supervisor 12x), and 18x P/E (was 20x): $124.21 and $112.32. Engine fair value $93.09 (was $73.02). (5) Ladder: 12-month moves are close to a random walk and narrative stocks can stay rich, so I centre on ~$128 (bear $72 at 30%, base $133 at 45%, bull $230 at 25%, ~27-30% dispersion within each). P(>= $152) = 0.371.

model_inputs.gap_note: Judgment calls for Kilian: (1) Multiples below his 15x / 27x and below the supervisor's 12x EV/EBITDA. Horizon NTM EBITDA is ~80% compute rent at ~2x the NPV-0 new-chip price ($18.8/W-yr at $38/W), earned by a fleet with a 6-year life on 90-day-terminable leases; neoclouds trade well below 10x 2027 EBITDA (CRWV market cap ~2.5x consensus 2027 EBITDA before debt). At 12x / 18x fair value is $103.71; at 15x / 27x, $131.13 (a departure of more than 5%). (2) Net debt at the horizon is stated directly ($69.6B) from a quarterly build. (3) Shares are economic: Musk's 1,302M Mars/100 TW-conditioned shares are excluded except a 5% re-cut probability (supervisor finding accepted). (4) The SOTP leg sits far below the multiple legs; the gap is the durability question itself.
